question: What is the primary physical nerve pathway connecting the gastrointestinal tract directly to the central nervous system?
explanation: The vagus nerve serves as the major physical and biochemical communication highway between the gut and the brain within the gut-brain axis. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h1)

question: How do diets rich in ultra-processed foods negatively impact mental health through the gut-brain axis?

options.A: By increasing gut permeability and systemic inflammation
options.B: By overstimulating the production of cerebrospinal fluid
options.C: By destroying all beneficial gut microbiota instantly
options.D: By blocking the physical absorption of water in the colon

explanation: Poor diets can compromise the gut lining, allowing inflammatory markers to circulate and impact central nervous system functioning. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h1)

question: Which symptom commonly seen in severe major depression leads directly to inadequate dietary intake and weight loss?
explanation: Depressive loss of pleasure and slowed physical movement often strip away the motivation and energy needed to acquire and consume food. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: A patient experiencing acute manic excitement is at highest risk for which nutritional complication?
explanation: Manic individuals burn vast amounts of energy through constant movement and frequently neglect basic fluid and food intake. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h2)

question: Which medication class is most frequently associated with significant weight gain, dyslipidemia, and insulin resistance?
explanation: Atypical or second-generation antipsychotics carry a heavy metabolic footprint, often leading to rapid weight gain and altered glucose metabolism. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: A patient starting lithium therapy complains of a persistent metallic taste and increased thirst. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Advise the patient to stop drinking water entirely
options.B: Encourage sugar-free fluids and monitor daily fluid balance
options.C: Instruct the patient to immediately discontinue the lithium
options.D: Recommend high-sodium energy drinks to replace minerals

explanation: Lithium causes thirst and metallic tastes; providing healthy fluid options maintains hydration without overloading the patient with high-sugar beverages. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of obtaining baseline anthropometric measurements in a newly admitted psychiatric patient?

options.A: To diagnose underlying hereditary psychiatric disorders instantly
options.B: To measure the exact electrical activity of the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: To accurately calculate the precise daily dosage of psychotherapy
options.D: To evaluate baseline weight and body mass index for changes

explanation: Anthropometric baselines like weight and BMI allow nurses to track nutritional decline or medication-induced weight gain over time. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h4)

question: Which assessment finding represents a biochemical indicator of poor nutritional status?
explanation: Serum albumin is a primary plasma protein used clinically to evaluate visceral protein status and chronic nutritional health. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h4)

question: Why should rigid calorie-counting sheets generally be avoided when teaching patients with acute psychiatric conditions?

options.A: They completely invalidate all biochemical laboratory findings
options.B: They are scientifically proven to have zero impact on human health
options.C: They require expensive electronic calculators unavailable in hospitals
options.D: They can trigger anxiety and obsessive-compulsive eating behaviors

explanation: Rigid tracking can exacerbate underlying anxiety or fuel disordered eating patterns, making simple visual models a safer educational approach. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h5)

question: What is an effective strategy when educating a psychiatric patient with severe executive dysfunction about nutrition?

options.A: Handing them a dense, highly technical textbook on metabolism
options.B: Involving family members or caregivers in the educational sessions
options.C: Requiring them to pass a written examination before every meal
options.D: Isolating them in a room until they memorize a complex meal plan

explanation: Cognitive and executive impairments make meal planning difficult, making caregiver involvement essential for practical success at home. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h5)

question: A hospitalized patient with schizophrenia refuses meals, expressing a firm belief that the food is poisoned. What is the most appropriate nursing intervention?

options.A: Withhold all food and water until the delusion naturally passes
options.B: Force-feed the patient immediately to prevent severe starvation
options.C: Offer factory-sealed packaged foods or allow family-brought meals
options.D: Tell the patient their paranoid delusion is completely ridiculous

explanation: Providing sealed or familiar foods respects the patient's anxiety and paranoia while safely ensuring they receive necessary nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h6)

question: What is an effective approach when addressing financial constraints during dietary counseling for vulnerable populations?

options.A: Demanding that they purchase imported organic specialty items
options.B: Insisting they hire a private chef for daily home cooking
options.C: Recommending affordable, nutrient-dense local food alternatives
options.D: Advising them to skip meals entirely to save household money

explanation: Practical nursing care respects economic realities by focusing on accessible, budget-friendly local ingredients that provide balanced nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h6)

question: Which professional is primarily responsible for designing specialized therapeutic meal plans within the healthcare team?
explanation: Registered dietitians possess specialized clinical training in designing targeted nutritional interventions and therapeutic meal plans. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h7)

question: Why is the nurse uniquely positioned to coordinate interprofessional dietary management for psychiatric inpatients?

options.A: Because nurses are the only team members permitted to interact with dietitians
options.B: Because nurses hold the exclusive legal authority to prescribe all medications
options.C: Because nurses maintain continuous daily contact and observe direct food intake
options.D: Because nurses handle the financial billing and grocery purchasing for the hospital

explanation: Constant bedside presence places the nurse in the best position to monitor actual eating habits, physical responses, and side effects. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T010#GNS227_U7_T010_h7)
